{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — E-Path FX Platform Licence Agreement

**To:** Deal Team
**From:** In-House Counsel (Customer/Licensee side)
**Re:** Playbook review of Licensor's draft — verified findings

---

## Executive Summary

We have completed a playbook review of the draft Licence Agreement. Of the eighteen rules assessed, six clauses are compliant and require no redline, nine are deviations requiring negotiation, and three rules are unaddressed in the document altogether.

The risk in this draft is concentrated in the allocation of liability and in our ability to exit. Two findings are critical. First, the only indemnity in the Agreement runs against us: Article XII requires Licensee to defend and indemnify Licensor, and there is no Licensor indemnity anywhere in the document, while Article XIII expressly excludes Licensor liability for infringement claims arising from use of the Licensed Technology. Second, Article XIII caps only Licensor's liability, at one half of amounts we have paid, while leaving our own liability uncapped. Each of these sits in walk-away territory on our playbook, and they compound one another.

The exit and control provisions are the next priority. We are committed to a 36-month Initial Period with no convenience termination right, Licensor may unilaterally extend that term by a further seven years at its sole option under Article IV, our licence automatically terminates on a Change of Control under Article XX(a), and Article XXII obliges us to disclose and offer Licensor a right to match any third-party offer for our assets or a merger. There is also no post-termination transition or data-return obligation on Licensor, notwithstanding that this is a hosted platform holding our trading data.

On the positive side, several commercially significant terms are already acceptable: the licence is expressly non-exclusive with no sourcing or non-compete restraint on us, pricing is purely usage-based with no minimum commitment or take-or-pay, there are no liquidated damages or early-termination fees payable by us, and governing law and venue sit at our preferred position (New York law, exclusive New York state and federal jurisdiction, no arbitration).

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | Confidential Information/Non-Solicitation (Art. XII, p0128–p0129; Art. XIII) |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Deviation | Confidential Information/Non-Solicitation (Art. XIII) |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | General Provisions (Art. XXIV(c); Art. XX(a)) |
| High | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions (Art. III; Art. VII(b); Art. XXI) |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions (Art. II.iii, p0041, p0045; Art. XX(a)) |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Missing | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions (Arts. IV, XIX, XX) |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | Confidential Information/Non-Solicitation |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § I Certain Definitions |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Deviation | Confidential Information/Non-Solicitation (Art. XXII, p0139–p0141) |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Deviation | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions (Art. IV, p0049) |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | Warranty Disclaimer (Art. VIX; p0093) |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Missing | Confidential Information/Non-Solicitation (Art. XXI) |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | Art. IV(b); p0064 |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Deviation | Confidential Information/Non-Solicitation (Art. X(b), p0125) |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | General Provisions (a), p0145–p0146 |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions | Compliant | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions (Art. V; Art. VII) |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | General Provisions (p0144–p0159) |

---

## Walk-Away Items

The following provisions fall into walk-away territory under our playbook and must move before we can sign:

1. **No Licensor indemnity, coupled with a one-way Licensee indemnity (Art. XII / Art. XIII).** We carry the defence and indemnity obligation for the exercise of our own licence rights, while Article XIII expressly provides that Licensor shall not be liable for infringement claims arising from use of the Licensed Technology. Our fallback ask is a Licensor IP indemnity with the customary modification, combination and specification exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies and a 3x annual fees super-cap, plus conforming "subject to Article XIII-A" edits so the retained exclusion and cap do not contradict the new indemnity.

2. **One-sided liability cap set below six months' fees (Art. XIII).** The cap applies only to Licensor and is set at one half of amounts paid, with our liability uncapped and expanded by Article XII and the Article II exculpations. Fallback: a mutual cap at fees paid in the 12 months preceding the claim, with indemnification, confidentiality breaches, gross negligence and wilful misconduct outside the cap.

3. **Automatic termination of the licence on our Change of Control (Art. XX(a)), with no assignment carve-outs (Art. XXIV(c)).** Licensor may refuse consent on competitive or subjective "adversely effected" grounds, and there is no affiliate or M&A carve-out and no restriction on Licensor assignment. We seek the preferred position: consent-free assignment to an Affiliate or M&A successor, consent (not unreasonably withheld) for Licensor assignments with no assignment to our competitors, and removal of the Licensor termination right on our change of control.

4. **Licensor's unilateral seven-year extension option (Art. IV, p0049).** Licensor may extend the 36-month Initial Period at its sole option with no Licensee consent and no non-renewal window — and this contradicts the same Article's own "mutual agreement in writing" language. We require renewal by mutual written agreement only.

5. **"AS IS" supply with no performance warranty (Art. VIX).** All warranties are disclaimed and Licensor expressly does not warrant that errors or nonconformity to the Documentation will be corrected; the commercially-reasonable-efforts Error Correction covenant at p0093 is not a substitute. Fallback: 90-day Software conformance warranty, 30-day services warranty, repair/replace/refund, with carve-outs from the disclaimer.

6. **No data return or transition assistance (Art. XXI).** Article XXI runs one way — our licences terminate and we return Licensor's property — with no obligation on Licensor to return our trading and market data held on its hosted platform. Fallback: at least 90 days' transition assistance and export of our data within 30 days of expiry or termination.

We also note two items that approach walk-away territory: the unlimited-frequency, no-notice audit right in Article IV(b), and the absence of any insurance covenant given that Licensor routes our market data and Spot FX trading activity through its platform.

---

## Next Steps

1. **Issue the redline.** Proposals are drafted and verified for all nine deviations and the three missing-clause insertions. The NOSOLICIT edit was repaired during verification and should be re-read before the draft goes out.
2. **Lead with the liability package.** Present INDEMN and LOL-CAP together as a single trade: a Licensor IP indemnity at a 3x annual fees super-cap in exchange for a mutual 12-month cap with the standard carve-outs. We have deliberately held back the preferred asks (USD 1,000,000 floor, "paid or payable", mutual consequential-damages exclusion, data protection/fraud/IP carve-outs, defence duty, affiliates and claim procedure) as trading room.
3. **Treat the exit cluster as one negotiation.** ASSIGN, LICENSE (Art. XX(a) automatic termination), T4C, RENEWAL, MFN (Art. XXII right of first refusal) and TRANSITION all bear on our ability to leave or to be acquired. Sequencing them together avoids conceding one and being met with another.
4. **Confirm the commercial position on deliverables.** The customization work and unique client front end we pay for under Article VII(b) currently vest in Licensor via the "Derivative Work" definition. Please confirm with the business how material those deliverables are, so we can calibrate between the fallback licence-back and a fuller ownership ask.
5. **Housekeeping to raise in any amendment.** Two non-material drafting points for the file: the Article V.III(b) reference to amounts payable "by the Licensor" where the payer is plainly the Licensee, and the now-deleted §XXIV(c) cross-reference to a non-existent "Section 13.4(a)".
6. **Flag for business, not legal.** The Field of Use is confined to Spot FX; extending it to other FX products would require Licensor's agreement. This is a commercial scoping question rather than a playbook deviation."}
